$comment: Pre-existing sink contracts that permit silence — scripts/check-optional-error-sink-contract.mjs (#9754).
Each entry is a sink type declaring an optional `error` with no GUARANTEED fallback channel.
SHRINK-ONLY and hand-edited under review. The checker fails on a stale entry, so a sink that
gets repaired must have its entry deleted in the same PR, and there is deliberately no
`--fix`/`--update` flag — a generator would let a NEW violation be admitted by 'just run the
update command', which is precisely how a gate stops meaning anything.
⛔ This file is NOT an exemption list and NOT a place to add new work. A newly written sink
with an optional `error` is a violation to fix, never a row to append. Every entry below
names WHY it is still here.
HISTORY, so the shrink is auditable rather than asserted:
17 red — the measured first-run population (36 sink types in packages/** declare `error`;
11 declare it REQUIRED; 8 declared it optional beside a REQUIRED `warn`).
-2     — #9754's own PR repaired `SweepLogger` (plugin-email) and `ProjectionLogger`
(plugin-security), and recorded the remaining 15 here.
-12     — #10556 paid down twelve of the thirteen mechanical repairs: cloud-connection,
metadata-protocol, plugin-approvals/lifecycle-hooks, both plugin-audit sinks,
both plugin-auth sinks, plugin-email/attachment-reclaim, plugin-reports,
plugin-sharing, plugin-webhooks and service-knowledge.
= 3    — what was left after #10556's first PR, and NONE of the three was left for lack
of effort: one was a serialisation leftover whose reason had expired
(approval-service.ts), and two are DESIGN calls escalated to the maintainer
rather than answered by a dev to make this checker green (security-plugin.ts,
settings-service.types.ts).
-1     — #10556's follow-up dispatch repaired the serialisation leftover once its
fence (PR #10547/#10739) cleared: `logger@ApprovalServiceOptions` dropped the
`?` from `warn`, mechanically identical to the twelve already paid down.
= 2    — both remaining rows are the escalated DESIGN calls; neither is a `?` deletion.
+3     — #11069 widened the POPULATION, not the tree. The checker now reads bare `Function`
as a channel, so three `plugin-sharing` sinks that were spelled
`{ info?: Function; warn?: Function; error?: Function; debug?: Function }` became
visible for the first time. All three were already red on the day this ledger was
first written; none is new code, and none was written after it.
⚠️ ON THAT +3, because it is the one line above that adds rows to a shrink-only file:
the ⛔ below forbids appending a NEWLY WRITTEN violation, which is what would let this
file launder new debt. It does not forbid recording a sink the checker previously could
not see. The distinction is the whole point: a measurement fix that had to stay silent
about what it measured would make widening the population cost more than leaving the
blind spot in, and the blind spot is what #11069 was filed about. The alternative —
flipping the three `warn`s — was ruled OUT of this card: all three options types are
PUBLICLY EXPORTED from `plugin-sharing`'s `index.ts`, so requiring `warn` breaks any host
passing `{ info, error }`. That is #10556's contract call. These rows exist to hand it a
decidable question instead of a silence.
-4     — #10556's RULED SHAPE (maintainer, 2026-08-24, three answers on one card).
(a) `logger@SecurityPlugin` — the `= {}` default became a console-backed
sink, loud until a host injects one; silent-by-declaration was
REJECTED. `warn` is now guaranteed and the shape moved to a named
`SecurityReportSink`, so the anonymous row is gone from the census.
(c) the three PUBLICLY EXPORTED `plugin-sharing` options types tightened
per #9754 — shipped `minor` with a changeset naming the
published-contract break for external hosts. Not a `?` deletion: they
were spelled with bare `Function`, so the members needed real
signatures (which is also what unblocks #10692's `MinimalLogger`).
= 1    — (b) `SettingsDiagnosticsLogger` STAYS, by the same ruling, as a recorded
deliberate exception. Its row's `note` carries the reason of record; read
it before treating this file's length as a worklist. There is no
mechanical repair left in here — the last one left in PR #10937.
Shrink-only is unaffected: each row still fails the gate the moment its sink stops being
red, so all three can only leave this file, never linger.

entries.note:
RECORDED DELIBERATE EXCEPTION — not unpaid debt, and not a worklist item. The maintainer ruled on 2026-08-24 (#10556 limb (b)) that this sink KEEPS its optional `warn`, and this row is where that ruling is recorded.

REASON OF RECORD — ASSIGNABILITY, and it is the type's own doc rather than a rationalisation added here. `service-settings` is framework-agnostic by design (it must never learn about the plugin context — see the file header), so a caller hands it `ctx.logger`, a spec `Logger`, `console.error` or a one-line spy interchangeably. Every member is declared with ONE string parameter and no `...rest`, because a `...rest: unknown[]` tail would not even accept the spec `Logger` this surface exists to accept: its `error(message, error?: Error, meta?)` is narrower than `unknown` in those positions, so the assignment fails contravariantly. Making `warn` REQUIRED costs 10 single-member `{ error }` spies across 6 test files their assignability (measured on #10556) and buys nothing here, because this module does not depend on the TYPE for its fallback: all three report sites in `settings-service.ts` are written `if (this.logger?.error) … else console.error(…)`, and `config-change-audit.ts` re-declares the channel locally as `SettingsDiagnosticsLogger & { warn?: (message: string) => void }`. The guaranteed channel is in the CODE, which is the one shape #9754's rule cannot read — so this is an exception to record, not a repair to schedule.

⚠️ MEASURED CORRECTION (2026-08-24, same PR): this row previously read `verdict: "no-fallback"` / `members: "{ error? }"` and described itself as "the ONLY `no-fallback` sink left in the tree". All three were stale. #10250 added a `warn?` member for the pre-bind READ report, so the checker renders this sink `optional-fallback` over `{ error? warn? }`, and the census line prints ZERO no-fallback sinks. The ruling's phrase "single-member `{error?}` surface" describes the shape on the day this row was written, not the day it was ruled on; the ruled ANSWER is unaffected, because the assignability reason above is about `warn` being OPTIONAL and is indifferent to whether `warn` is declared at all. Corrected here rather than left, because a ledger row asserting a verdict the gate no longer renders is precisely the un-re-measured claim this file's header exists to refuse. The row's IDENTITY is untouched: the checker keys on `file::sink` alone (`baselineKey`), and neither changed.
